shared_elements: horizontal band containing a row of repeated vertical strokes (comb-like)
repeated arc/hook motifs along an edge
monochrome figures on a bare stone ground
justification: The most specific correspondence is that each surface contains a long horizontal band filled with a row of closely spaced vertical strokes (a comb-like register in A, the crew strokes of the large hull in B), plus tiny schematic human figures and profile animal heads set against plain stone. Against that, A is a deeply modelled, three-dimensional relief on an upright rectangular pillar stacked in vertical registers, whereas B is a flat, purely linear outline drawing spread laterally across a rock face and dominated by a single boat form, so the manner of rendering and the overall compositional logic are quite different.
